fields.title: Herniated disc
fields.bodyHtml:
Herniated disc: innovative treatment in Israel

A herniated disc is a common condition that can cause severe pain, numbness or weakness because of pressure on the spinal nerves. In Israel, patients are offered advanced methods of diagnosing and treating a herniated disc that bring rapid relief of symptoms and recovery.

Diagnosis of a herniated disc

  1. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    The gold standard in diagnosis, allowing the position and size of the hernia to be established precisely.
  2. CT (computed tomography)
    May be used to obtain detailed images of the bony structures of the spine.
  3. Myelography
    A contrast study that may be used to assess the state of the spinal canal and the nerve roots.
  4. Electromyography (EMG)
    Carried out to assess the electrical activity of the muscles and nerves, which helps establish the extent of nerve damage.

Treatments for a herniated disc in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment
    Includes physiotherapy, pain-relieving medication, the use of braces and nerve blocks. It is aimed at reducing pain and inflammation and at strengthening the supporting muscles.
  2. Endoscopic discectomy — a minimally invasive surgical procedure with very rapid recovery, intended to relieve back pain caused by a herniated disc. This treatment is particularly effective for patients whose pain does not improve with conservative treatment.
  3. Minimally invasive techniques
    Such as percutaneous laser discectomy, radiofrequency ablation and endoscopic removal of the hernia, which offer an alternative to open surgery with a lower risk of complications and a shorter recovery period.
  4. Surgery
    Laminectomy, discectomy or spinal fusion may be recommended where conservative treatment brings no relief and the hernia is causing serious neurological symptoms.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Individual treatment plans are drawn up by a team of specialists including orthopaedic surgeons, neurologists and physiotherapists.
  • Advanced technology
    Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern devices for carrying out diagnostic and treatment procedures.
  • Experienced specialists
    Doctors with international recognition and extensive experience in treating conditions of the spine.
  • A focus on quality of life
    The main emphasis is not only on relieving pain and restoring function but also on improving patients' overall quality of life.

Treatment of a herniated disc in Israel gives patients access to innovative therapies that achieve a considerable improvement without a long recovery. An individual approach to every case ensures the best choice of treatment, based on the patient's particular needs and expectations.

fields.title: Peritoneal mesothelioma
fields.bodyHtml:
Peritoneal mesothelioma: advanced treatment in Israel

Mesothelioma of the peritoneum, also known as peritoneal mesothelioma, is a rare type of cancer arising in the membrane that lines the abdominal cavity. This type of cancer is often associated with exposure to asbestos. Clinics in Israel offer a comprehensive approach to treating this condition using modern methods of diagnosis and treatment.

Diagnosis of peritoneal mesothelioma:

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    These imaging methods allow the extent of the tumour within the abdominal cavity to be assessed.
  2. PET-CT: Provides a detailed picture of the metabolic activity of the tumour and of any metastases.
  3. Biopsy:
    Taking tissue samples for histological examination — the gold standard for confirming a diagnosis of mesothelioma.
  4. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests can identify markers associated with mesothelioma, such as mesothelin.

Treatments for peritoneal mesothelioma:

  1. Chemotherapy:
    • Systemic chemotherapy: The use of anti-cancer medicines to destroy the cancer cells.
    • Intraperitoneal chemotherapy: Chemotherapy medicines delivered directly into the abdominal cavity for local treatment.
  2. Surgery:
    • Cytoreductive surgery: Removal of as much tumour tissue as possible.
    • Peritonectomy: Removal of the affected peritoneum to reduce the bulk of the tumour and ease symptoms.
  3. Hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC):
    • After the visible tumours have been removed, the peritoneum is treated with heated chemotherapy medicines to destroy any remaining cancer cells.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: A team of specialists including oncologists, surgeons and radiologists ensures a comprehensive approach to every case.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of modern technology for diagnosis and treatment improves results and shortens recovery time.
  • Individualised treatment: Treatment plans are drawn up taking account of the particular features of the condition and the patient's general health.

Treatment of peritoneal mesothelioma in Israel aims to extend patients' life expectancy and quality of life as far as possible, drawing on the latest advances in medical science and practice.

fields.title: Mydriasis
fields.bodyHtml:
General information about mydriasis

Mydriasis is a condition in which the pupil is dilated. Normally the pupil dilates in darkness or in stressful situations, but mydriasis can be caused by various illnesses, injuries or the effects of medicines. Pathological mydriasis requires diagnosis and treatment, since it may indicate serious disturbances in the body.

Causes of mydriasis

  1. Neurological disorders: damage to the cranial nerves, stroke, raised intracranial pressure.
  2. Eye injuries: bruising, damage to the iris.
  3. Infections: meningitis, encephalitis.
  4. Toxic substances: poisoning by drugs, alcohol or chemicals.
  5. Medicines: antidepressants, antihistamines, eye drops containing atropine.
  6. Other conditions: glaucoma, brain tumours.

Diagnosis of mydriasis

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about the symptoms, any preceding illness, previous conditions and treatment, and possible injuries or exposure to toxic substances.
  2. Visual examination and ophthalmoscopy:
    • The ophthalmologist examines the patient's pupils, noting their reaction to light, their symmetry and any other changes. Ophthalmoscopy allows assessment of the optic nerve, the vessels of the fundus and the retina.
  3. Gonioscopy:
    • Examination of the angle of the anterior chamber of the eye using a special contact lens. This method helps identify causes of impaired drainage in the eye, which may be linked to glaucoma.
  4. Visual field test:
    • A computerised perimeter is used to check the patient's peripheral vision, to identify any restriction and establish the extent of damage to the optic nerve.
  5. Optical coherence tomography (OCT):
    • A scan of the eye that produces high-quality images of the structures of the fundus, including the optic nerve and the retina.
  6. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT):
    • These imaging methods are used to identify possible structural changes in the brain that may be the cause of the mydriasis.
  7. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood and urine tests can help identify toxins or infections that may have caused the mydriasis.

Treatment of mydriasis

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Antibiotics or antiviral medicines: where the mydriasis has an infectious cause (meningitis or encephalitis, for example).
    • Antidotes and detoxification: in cases of poisoning by toxic substances or medicines.
    • Eye drops: depending on the cause of the mydriasis, drops may be prescribed to lower the pressure inside the eye or improve drainage of fluid from it.
  2. Treatment of the underlying condition:
    • Where there is a neurological disorder (stroke or raised intracranial pressure, for example), appropriate treatment is given under the supervision of a neurologist.
  3. Surgery:
    • In rare cases, where the mydriasis is caused by structural changes in the eye or brain, surgical treatment may be required.
  4. Physiotherapy and rehabilitation:
    • Physiotherapy techniques and rehabilitation programmes may be used to restore the function of the eye and improve the patient's general condition.

Advantages of treating mydriasis in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating mydriasis and other eye conditions.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including laser technology and genetic testing.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of mydriasis in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.

fields.title: Myeloma
fields.bodyHtml:
Myeloma: advanced treatment in Israel

Myeloma, also known as multiple myeloma, is a type of blood cancer affecting the plasma cells in the bone marrow. In Israel, patients with myeloma are offered modern methods of diagnosis and innovative approaches to treatment, aimed at improving both the outlook and quality of life.

Diagnosis of myeloma

  1. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, measurement of protein levels including immunoglobulins and Bence Jones protein in the urine, and biochemical tests to assess kidney function and calcium levels.
  2. Bone marrow biopsy
    A procedure that establishes the presence of cancer cells and assesses how far the bone marrow is affected.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. X-rays of the skeleton
    These help identify areas of bone damage.
  4. MRI and CT
    Highly accurate imaging methods used for a more detailed examination of the affected areas.
  5. PET-CT
    One of the most modern diagnostic methods, allowing the activity of the disease in the body to be assessed.

Treatment of myeloma

  1. Chemotherapy
    The main treatment, aimed at destroying the cancer cells.
  2. Targeted therapy
    The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  3. Immunotherapy
    Includes the use of monoclonal antibodies and other medicines to stimulate the immune system against the cancer cells.
  4. Bone marrow transplant
    A procedure that restores healthy bone marrow after intensive chemotherapy.
  5. Radiotherapy
    Used to relieve pain and treat individual areas of bone damage.
  6. Bisphosphonates
    Medicines that strengthen the bones and prevent the fractures myeloma can cause.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: treatment involves oncologists, haematologists, radiologists, bone marrow transplant specialists and other doctors.
  • Individualised treatment: the treatment plan is drawn up taking account of the genetic and molecular features of each patient's disease.
  • Innovative treatments: access to the latest developments in medicine, including the newest medicines and therapeutic strategies.
  • A high standard of medical care: modern clinics equipped with advanced technology, and highly qualified medical staff.

Treatment of myeloma in Israel combines highly qualified specialists, the use of advanced technology and an individual approach to every patient, which helps achieve the best results and a considerable improvement in quality of life.
